sections.h2: Who bills property tax on a house in the city of St. Charles?
sections.html:
St. Charles County bills it. The city of St. Charles sets its own rate, but the county Assessor supplies the value and the county Collector sends one combined bill and takes payment. City Hall does not collect real estate tax.

  • Value and classification: St. Charles County Assessor, 201 N. Second Street, 636-949-7425.
  • Bills and payments: St. Charles County Collector of Revenue, Suite 134 at the same address, 636-949-7470.
  • City rate questions: the city Finance Department. The city's FAQ says the City Council sets the actual rate each August.

The city also mails a projected tax liability notice after values change. It is a forecast of what the change in assessed value could mean for the coming year and the city's FAQ states plainly that it is not a bill, so no money should be sent. Your actual bill carries a line for every district that taxes the address, including the state, county, school, fire, ambulance and library.

sections.h2: What is the city of St. Charles like for a home seller?
sections.html:
St. Charles is the seat of St. Charles County, about 20 miles northwest of downtown St. Louis on the Missouri River near where it meets the Mississippi. French Canadian fur trader Louis Blanchette settled it around 1769 as Les Petites Cotes, and it was the first capital of Missouri from 1821 to 1826. It is the eighth most populous city in the state (Wikipedia).

Wikipedia describes a historic shopping district on Main Street and rapid new home construction, commercial growth and population growth since the late 1970s. The Census QuickFacts page gives 72,561 residents for July 2025 and 30,362 households. Owners occupy 68.0% of homes, the median owned home was valued at $298,700 for 2020 to 2024, median gross rent was $1,251, and median household income was $85,937. Workers average 21.6 minutes to get to a job.

Most of the city is in the City of St. Charles School District, which runs St. Charles High School and St. Charles West. Southern neighborhoods belong to the Francis Howell district and northern ones to Orchard Farm, so check the district named on your bill before you describe a home to buyers. Lindenwood University and the riverfront Family Arena are among the local draws.

sections.h2: What does the county tax calendar mean for a St. Charles seller?
sections.html:
Bills are issued by December 1 and are due December 31, and anything received on or after January 1 picks up penalty and interest. Real estate is revalued in odd-numbered years, so a 2027 reassessment is coming, and notices are mailed in April.

If you want to contest a value, request an informal hearing with the Assessor first, then file with the Board of Equalization by 5 p.m. on the second Monday in July. That date passed on July 13, 2026 and the next is July 12, 2027. The State Tax Commission is the last step. The county appeal page has the forms and contacts, and the county guide says to schedule the informal hearing within 10 days of the notice mailing date.

The county guide adds one rule that matters at closing. The party holding title at the end of the tax year is responsible for that year's real estate tax, and taxes are often prorated between buyer and seller at closing. Ask the title company to show how it handled the proration before you sign.

sections.h2: Which city programs show up on a St. Charles tax bill?
sections.html:
Two voter-approved programs are collected on the county real estate tax bill for houses inside the city limits. Both pay for repairs to the pipes between the house and the public line, which can be a real expense in an older neighborhood.

City of St. Charles line and lateral programs listed on the city's FAQ
ProgramYearly chargePaysUnits covered
Sewer lateral repair$2090% of the lowest of three bids, up to $7,500Up to 6
Residential water line insurance$12100% of the lowest of three bids, up to $3,000Up to 4

Owners are enrolled automatically and cannot opt out, and houses outside the city limits are not eligible. The sewer program covers the pipe from the exterior wall to the city main. The water program covers the line from the meter or first shut-off valve to the exterior wall. A buyer who asks about either one can be pointed to the city's Public Works Department, or Collections and Billing at 636-949-3212 for the water line.

sections.h2: What must a seller do under the St. Charles real estate disclosure ordinance?
sections.html:
The seller must complete and sign a city disclosure form for every residential sale inside the city. Ordinance 23-062 was passed on June 6, 2023 and took effect September 1, 2023, so it applies to any closing now (city disclosure page).

The form is notarized at closing and a copy goes to the city, which collects it through an online survey link. It does not need to be recorded. Its purpose is to tell the incoming owner about city rules, including:

  • Building and sign permits and required inspections.
  • Recreational vehicle and boat parking and storage, fencing and property maintenance.
  • Solid waste collection, short term rentals and floodplain development.
  • Historic preservation districts, site plan and architectural review, and zoning restrictions.

Call Community Development at 636-949-3222 with questions. Your title company or agent will usually carry the form, but confirm it is on the closing checklist.

sections.h2: Do repairs or rentals in St. Charles need city approval before you sell?
sections.html:
Some do. The Building Division lists projects that need permits, among them decks, additions, basement finishing, electrical or plumbing changes, a water heater or air conditioning and heating unit replacement, a new sewer lateral and fences taller than 6 feet. Painting, new flooring, a new faucet, roof shingles and siding replacement do not need a permit. Call 636-949-3227 to schedule an inspection.

Rentals have their own rules. Residential occupancy inspections are required for long term rentals before the first tenant moves in and between tenants. For short term rentals, a 2025 amendment limited new residential permits to the Extended Historic Preservation District and cut the cap to 0.15% of housing units, up to 48 residential units. The city reports it is at that maximum and is not accepting new residential applications, and the city page tells owners to call St. Charles County at 636-949-7900 about property tax effects. A buyer who plans to run a short term rental should verify zoning first at 636-949-3222.

Exterior changes in the historic district need approval from the Historic Landmarks Preservation and Architectural Review Board, according to the city's FAQ.

sections.h2: How does the St. Charles climate and permit record affect a house?
sections.html:
The city has a humid subtropical climate with warm summers and cool winters. Average annual precipitation is 45.71 inches, spring is the wettest season, and the record high is 115 degrees and the record low is minus 25 (Wikipedia climate table). Heat, humidity and spring storms are part of owning here, so gather repair records for the roof, cooling system and water heater before you list.

The Assessor checks structure measurements against building permits, and new construction is added to the rolls every year. Keep permits for any finished basement, deck or addition together, since those are the projects the Building Division says need one.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property tax if I live in St. Charles?
faqs.a: Pay the St. Charles County Collector of Revenue at 201 N. Second Street, by phone at 1-855-227-7840, or online at stcharlesmocollector.org. The city itself does not take real estate tax payments.

faqs.q: Is the projected tax notice from the city a bill?
faqs.a: No. The city's FAQ says the notice is an estimate of possible liability after an assessment change and tells owners not to send money. The real bill comes later in the year from the county.

faqs.q: Do I have to file the disclosure when I sell a house in St. Charles?
faqs.a: Yes, for any residential sale inside the city after September 1, 2023. The seller signs it, it is notarized at closing, and a copy goes to the city. It is not recorded.

faqs.q: Can I opt out of the sewer lateral charge in St. Charles?
faqs.a: No. Voters approved the program, so every eligible home inside the city limits pays the $20 yearly charge and is enrolled. The city's FAQ says the same of the $12 water line program.

faqs.q: How do I challenge my St. Charles assessment?
faqs.a: Ask the county Assessor for an informal hearing, then file with the Board of Equalization by 5 p.m. on the second Monday in July. The next deadline is July 12, 2027. Further appeal goes to the State Tax Commission.
